title: Rental Month Caps and Oxygen Lifetime by Payer Class (Insurance Coverage & Patient Responsibility)
content:
The payer class of the patient's **Insurance Coverage & Patient Responsibility** record fixes three counts used by the rental equipment lines: the paid months after which a capped-rental item transfers to the patient, the paid oxygen equipment months after which equipment payments stop, and the useful lifetime of oxygen equipment.

| Payer class | Capped-rental months to title | Oxygen equipment payment cap (months) | Oxygen equipment useful lifetime (months) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Original Medicare Part B | 13 | 36 | 60 |
| Medicare Advantage HMO | 13 | 36 | 60 |
| Medicare Advantage PPO | 13 | 36 | 60 |
| Medicaid Fee-for-Service | 10 | 36 | 60 |
| Commercial HMO | 10 | 36 | 60 |
| Commercial PPO | 10 | 36 | 60 |
| Medicare Supplement Plan G | 13 | 36 | 60 |

## Meaning of each count

- **Capped-rental months to title**: the number of paid rental months in one continuous rental period after which title of a capped-rental item transfers to the patient.
- **Oxygen equipment payment cap**: the number of paid monthly oxygen equipment payments after which equipment payments stop for the oxygen rental period.
- **Oxygen equipment useful lifetime**: the reasonable useful lifetime of oxygen equipment counted from the first day of the first paid month, during which the supplier must keep furnishing the equipment.

## Illustration (hypothetical)

A capped-rental item rented under Commercial HMO transfers to the patient after the 10th paid month of one continuous rental period; the same item under Medicare Advantage PPO transfers after the 13th. The oxygen counts are the same in every class: payments stop after 36 paid months, and the equipment is furnished until 60 months have run from the first day of the first paid month.
